text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet raised petrol prices for a second time in as many weeks, effective today. Prices rose by 10.9 percent after a 15 percent hike on September 27.
-- Greek police has arrested four Bulgarians and two Iraqis on charges of forged passports traffic after it found 77 fake passports in a flat in Greece's capital Atina.
-- Bulgaria's Kozlodui nuclear power plant received a fresh shipment of Russian nuclear fuel on Thursday, Energy minister Roumen Ovcharov said.

-- Foreign investors, members of the Bulgarian International Business Association (BIBA) demanded clearer regulations for the tax benefits they have been granted recently under amendments to Bulgaria's Foreign Invetment Law.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to cut the oil refinery Neftohim's capital by 18.966 million levs as Neftohim had to transfer its stake in the Bank Consolidation Company to the Ministry of Economic Development under an earlier government decision.
-- Iraq is ready to repay its $2 billion debt to Bulgaria if the UN Sanctions Committee approves the operation, Bulgaria's Industry Minister Lyubomir Dachev said.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank allowed 10 commercial banks, which previously have pledged to curtail giving fresh credits to extend loans to farmers for the autumn sowing.
-- Interior ministry armed forces joined police patrols in Sofia streets on Thursday to boost security, the ministry said.
-- Bulgaria's foreign exchange reserves fell to $506.3 million in September from $575 million in August, the Bulgarian National Bank said.
-- Russia's ambassador in Bulgaria Alexander Avdeyev said that "certain groupings" in Bulgaria hindered Russia's gas giant Gazprom's business.
Russia has waited for Bulgaria's agreement to grant gas pipeline concessions to Gazprom too long, Avdeyev said after talks with one of Bulgaria's presidential candidates.
-- South Korea's Daewoo Corp said it had launched a subsidiary in Bulgaria in a move to step up its activities in this Balkan country.
The corporation is interested in Bulgaria's banking sector, chemical industry, telecommunication, machine building and tourism, the representative of Daewoo's Sofia branch office Chung-Hwan Kim said.
